title: Seated Cable Row
summary: A seated cable row for the upper back and lats.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: seated cable row station or cable station with an adjustable pulley.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.8 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.5 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.4 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.

setup.text: Sit with your feet on the platform and your knees slightly bent, holding the handle.
Sit tall and let your arms stretch forward.
Pull the handle to your stomach, bringing your shoulder blades back.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.

form_cues.cue: Sit tall with a neutral spine
Pull the handle to your stomach
Let your shoulders reach forward on the return
Keep your torso nearly still, with only a small lean, and let your arms do the moving.

mistakes.text: Rocking far back and forth to move the stack.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Less upper-back focus, One side at a time.
